text:
vikram: Heads-up — saw steady memory growth on the kv cache when running a 30k-token chat sim. Growth seems correlated with lots of short-lived allocations (<= 256B) in the slab allocator, and we end up with a ton of tiny holes.

sara: ugh that sounds like the micro-frag pattern we saw last quarter. Any flamegraphs/profiles?

vikram: attached a quick heap profile snippet (filtered). Noting allocator hot paths and sample counts: 
```
# heap summary
512B slots: allocated 1.2M, free 320k, frag_ratio 2.75
4KB slabs: allocated 48k, free 22k, frag_ratio 1.18
avg hole size ~ 192 bytes
```
I think the block-size bucketing is too coarse for small kv entries (short prompt prefixes + small system tokens).

olivia: Interesting. Are these short-lived because of prefix churn or because we split large kvs into many mini-blocks?

vikram: both. Long contexts cause lots of KV writes and then partial deletes during eviction/paging. Two problems: allocator uses 256B min chunk which is okay but freelist gets lots of 192B holes due to header rounding, and reuse heuristic prefers same-size buckets but ignores locality, so we keep scattering tiny allocations across slabs.

tom: proposal: try a micro-scrub pass that does two things: 1) coalesce adjacent free mini-blocks in-place, 2) compact small live entries into fewer larger slots when CPU idle. Low-risk config toggles.

vikram: sketched a quick config idea:
```
kv.compactor.enabled = true
kv.compactor.sweep_interval_ms = 5000
kv.compactor.max_pause_ms = 3   # budget per shard
kv.compactor.coalesce_threshold = 512
kv.compactor.hot_merge_enabled = true
```
Would run on background thread per-shard with a tight max pause.

sara: sounds reasonable. Main concerns: 1) extra CPU during heavy traffic, 2) latency jitter if we do a big merge. How to measure risks?

vikram: suggested instrumentation: token-p99 before/after, per-shard CPU%, latency histograms during scrubs, and a metric for "holes_coalesced/sec". Also keep a kill-switch that disables merge when p99 > SLO.

olivia: can we do a cheaper path first: change allocator bucket sizing for small objects from 256B buckets to a mixed 128/256 strategy to reduce header waste? That should avoid doing compaction at all in many cases.

tom: yes — lower-touch option is to add a sub-bucket for <= 128B objects. Tradeoffs: more freelists, slightly more metadata. But CPU impact almost nil. I'd prefer trying the sub-bucket patch first, then micro-scrub if still issues.

vikram: agreed. I'll prototype sub-bucket and run the long-context sim for 6h. If we still see >5% mem growth vs baseline, fall back to scrub approach.

ci-bot: perf-run queued: run_id=kv-frag-subbucket-2333, est_time=4h. Config: sub_buckets=true, scrub=false.

vikram: quick note — we should also audit the eviction heuristic. Right now it's LRU-ish but doesn't prefer consolidating contiguous KV pages for reuse; evicting interleaved keys causes fragmentation. Maybe add a locality-aware eviction pass.

olivia: yep. Could tag pages with affinity IDs (conversation_id modulo some hash) and prefer evicting least-used pages with low affinity score so we don't leave many half-full pages.

tom: sketch for affinity scoring: score = alpha * recency + beta * (1 - occupancy_fragmentation). We can tune alpha/beta with a small A/B rollout.

vikram: action items:
- vikram: prototype sub-bucket allocator + run long sim (ci-bot queued)
- tom: draft micro-scrubber implementation plan + perf safety budget (max_pause)
- olivia: write eviction affinity RFC (short) with scoring equations and test vectors
- sara: prepare dashboards: mem-growth, holes_coalesced, p99 tokens, scrub_cpu%

sara: I'll add dashboard panels and a canary alert that flips when mem-growth over 1h > 2% AND p99 increases.

vikram: thanks. Will post perf outputs when run finishes. If sub-buckets fix > 80% of cases we avoid compactor complexity which is ideal.

olivia: TL;DR: try small allocator tweak first, prefer cheap fix. If not, micro-scrub and locality-aware eviction as follow-ups. :thumbsup:

tom: +1. Also, add unit tests for coalescing invariants before enabling scrub in mainline.

ci-bot: perf-run completed: run_id=kv-frag-subbucket-2333, status=PASS, mem_growth=0.9%, p99_delta=+0.02%

vikram: awesome — results look promising. I'll open a PR for sub-buckets and include the perf run logs.

sara: sweet. Merge window?

vikram: aiming for tomorrow's patch window. If anyone wants to review early ping me.

olivia: will take a look. cheers.
